hoche:1866.author: Nicomachus of Gerasa (ed. Richard Hoche)
hoche:1866.work: Nicomachi Geraseni Pythagorei Introductionis Arithmeticae Libri II
hoche:1866.locus: Leipzig: B. G. Teubner, 1866 (pp. i–xi, 1–147; CTS urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0358.tlg001.1st1K-grc1)
hoche:1866.note: Standard critical Teubner Greek edition collated from Munich (Cizensis, Monacensis G), Göttingen, Hamburg, and Paris manuscripts, preserving ancient α-pebble figurate diagrams and the synoptic table of Ten Means.

dooge:1926.author: Martin Luther D'Ooge (trans.), with F. E. Robbins & L. C. Karpinski
dooge:1926.work: Nicomachus of Gerasa: Introduction to Arithmetic
dooge:1926.locus: New York: Macmillan / University of Michigan Studies, Humanistic Series Vol. XVI, 1926 (pp. 181–286)
dooge:1926.note: First English translation of Nicomachus (Public Domain: published 1926, >95 years in US), accompanied by Studies in Greek Arithmetic (pp. 3–177) and critical mathematical footnotes.

boethius:friedlein:1867.author: Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius (ed. Gottfried Friedlein)
boethius:friedlein:1867.work: De Institutione Arithmetica Libri Duo, De Institutione Musica Libri Quinque
boethius:friedlein:1867.note: Boethius's authoritative Latin adaptation of Nicomachus, coining the term quadrivium (I.1, p. 7 Friedlein) and transmitting Nicomachean ratio species, equality unfolding, figurate numbers, and the Ten Means to the Latin West.

iamblichus:pistelli:1894.author: Iamblichus of Chalcis (ed. Ermenegildo Pistelli)
iamblichus:pistelli:1894.note: Fourth book of Iamblichus's On Pythagoreanism, preserving crucial historical testimonies on Archytas, Eudoxus, Hippasus, Myonides, Euphranor, and Eratosthenes' equality rule.

philoponus:hoche:1864.author: John Philoponus (ed. Richard Hoche)
philoponus:hoche:1864.work: Ioannis Philoponi in Nicomachi Arithmeticam Introductionem Libri Duo
philoponus:hoche:1864.note: Extensive Alexandrian Neoplatonic lecture commentary on Books I and II of Nicomachus edited by Richard Hoche immediately prior to his 1866 Teubner edition.

theon:hiller:1878.author: Theon of Smyrna (ed. Eduard Hiller)
theon:hiller:1878.work: Expositio Rerum Mathematicarum ad Legendum Platonem Utilium
theon:hiller:1878.locus: Leipzig: B. G. Teubner, 1878 (pp. 107–111 on Adrastos & Equality)
theon:hiller:1878.note: Parallel Middle Platonic mathematical handbook preserving Adrastos of Aphrodisias's proof of the three-term equality unfolding and side-and-diagonal numbers.

archytas:dk47b1.author: Archytas of Tarentum
archytas:dk47b1.locus: apud Nicomachum I.3.4 (Hoche pp. 6–7) & Porphyry In Ptol. Harm.
archytas:dk47b1.note: Authentic Doric fragment quoted by Nicomachus declaring astronomy, geometry, arithmetic, and music to be 'sister sciences' (ἀδελφεαὶ τὰ μαθήματα), plus definition of the three classical means.

plato:timaeus:27d-36d.author: Plato
plato:timaeus:27d-36d.note: Quoted verbatim by Nicomachus at I.2.3 (27d: eternal Being vs. continual Becoming) and expounded across II.18–29 (Same & Other, two cubic means, and harmonic division of the World-Soul).

plato:rep:vii-525a-534e.author: Plato
plato:rep:vii-525a-534e.note: Quoted by Nicomachus at I.3.7 (527d–e: purifying the 'eye of the soul' blinded by other pursuits) and II.24 (Nuptial Number).

plato:epinomis:991d-992a.author: Plato (or Philip of Opus)
plato:epinomis:991d-992a.note: Quoted by Nicomachus at I.3.5 on the 'single natural bond' (δεσμὸς πεφυκώς) uniting all mathematical sciences and rendering the learner blessed.

aristotle:cat:4b20.author: Aristotle
aristotle:cat:4b20.note: Foundational distinction between discrete and continuous quantity and ontological priority by non-reciprocal elimination (συναναιρεῖ μὲν, οὐ συναναιρεῖται δέ) underlying Nicomachus I.2–5.

euclid:elements:vii-ix.author: Euclid
euclid:elements:vii-ix.note: Euclidean deductive counterparts to Nicomachus: mutual subtraction/anthyphairesis (VII.1–2), infinitude of primes (IX.20), geometric series sum & even perfect numbers (IX.35–36), and geometric mean construction (VI.13).

pappus:synagoge:iii.author: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus:synagoge:iii.note: Constructive geometric synthesis of the three classical means in a single semicircle and systematic geometric derivation of all ten Nicomachean means.

proclus:in-euclid:35-37.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-euclid:35-37.work: Commentary on the First Book of Euclid's Elements
proclus:in-euclid:35-37.locus: Prologue I, Ch. XII, Friedlein pp. 35–37 (`geometor/proclus`)
proclus:in-euclid:35-37.note: Reproduces Nicomachus's exact Pythagorean fourfold schema of discrete (per se / ad aliud) and continuous (stationary / moving) quantity.

aquinas:in-boethium-trinitate.author: Thomas Aquinas
aquinas:in-boethium-trinitate.note: Scholastic epistemology of the Quadrivium, intelligible matter, and subalternation of music to arithmetic and astronomy to geometry.

pacioli:divina-proportione:1509.author: Luca Pacioli
pacioli:divina-proportione:1509.work: Summa de Arithmetica (1494) & De Divina Proportione (1509)
pacioli:divina-proportione:1509.note: Renaissance culmination of Boethian–Nicomachean proportion terminology alongside Euclid's extreme and mean ratio.

heath:hgm:1921.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:hgm:1921.work: A History of Greek Mathematics, Vol. I: From Thales to Euclid
heath:hgm:1921.note: Authoritative modern algebraic analysis of Nicomachus's Introductio Arithmetica, gnomon recurrences, sum of cubes, and Ten Means.
